sections.heading: The Owner Looks at Your House and Prices It
body: Redoing the outside of a house is a big spend, and most of us only do it once or twice. You want the person who writes the number to be the person who stands behind it.
That's me. I come out, walk around the house with you, and tell you what needs doing and what doesn't. Then I write the price for that work and nothing else.
The crew finishes the job, and I stop by while it's going on to make sure it's right.
That is the whole idea of Greenway. A price for the house in front of us, from the person who looked at it.

sections.heading: Window Replacement
body: Most people call about windows because of a room that never gets comfortable. Maybe there's fog between the panes, a draft at the sill, or a sash that fights you every time you open it.
Each of those means the window has stopped doing its job. The seal around the glass has failed or the frame has worn out, and you're heating and cooling the outdoors through it.
We replace one window or every window in the house. We also do basement and egress windows, sliding glass doors and entry doors, so the glass and frames on the house match.

sections.quote: And the windows are SO BEAUTIFUL!!!!!! The difference in the house staying warm is amazing too, the heater hardly kicks on now lol and the price, we compared 6 other companies and he blew them out of the water with the same quality and way better price.

sections.heading: Siding Replacement and Repair
body: Siding takes the Kansas wind, hail and summer sun before anything else on the house does. When it wears out you can see it: cracks, warped or loose pieces, faded panels, a stain on the ceiling inside.
What you can't see is the wall behind it, which is where the water goes when siding stops shedding it.
You don't always need the whole house done. If three walls are fine and one is shot, we'll tell you so and price the one. When the whole house does need it, the old siding leaves with us.
We also repair siding: rotted boards, storm damage and chimney siding.

sections.heading: Trim, Gutters and Paint
body: Windows and siding meet the roof edge, the gutters and the paint at the same lines. If you replace one and leave the rest, the old pieces stand out next to the new ones.

So we do fascia, soffit and trim along with your siding, put up new gutters and gutter protection, and paint the exterior as part of the same job. One crew, one schedule, one set of colors chosen together.
None of it has to be done at once. If the budget says windows now and siding next year, plan it that way and we'll make the second job fit the first.

sections.quote: John and his crew did an amazing job! They were 10k less than other quotes I got and John worked hard to get my project done on time and in budget and worked my project in quick! We had new siding, gutters, paint.. my house looks like a totally different house and beautiful!

sections.heading: One Company for the Whole Outside
body: Water doesn't care which part of the house it gets past. A gap at a window, a loose piece of siding and a sagging gutter can all send it to the same wall.

That's why we do all of it, and why I look at the whole house even when you call about one window. A leak at a window sill is often a siding or flashing problem, and you should know that before you pay to replace the window.
Do the whole exterior at once or one project at a time. Either way, you get one company to call.

sections.heading: Fog, Drafts, Noise and Windows That Stick
body: You usually know a window is finished before you can say why. A room that never gets comfortable. Curtains that move with the window shut.
A sash you have to bang to open, or one that won't stay up.

Fog or a haze between the two panes is the clearest sign. Modern windows are sealed double panes with gas between the glass, and when the seal fails the gas leaks out and moist air gets in. The glass can't be cleaned from the inside, and it no longer insulates the way it did.
Drafts and noise mean the same thing from another direction. The frame, the weatherstripping or the seal around the glass has worn out, so air and sound come straight through.
You end up paying to heat and cool the outdoors.

sections.heading: Why Old Windows Quit
body: Builder-grade windows are made to a price. The glass seals, the balances that hold a sash up and the plastic or aluminum frames wear out, often after fifteen or twenty years, sometimes sooner on the south and west sides of a Wichita house that take the sun and wind.
Repainting or re-caulking can slow a leak, but it can't fix a seal inside a sealed glass unit or a frame that has warped. Once the glass has fogged, the unit is done.
That is why the fix is usually a new window and not a repair. You don't have to replace every window at once. If only the bedroom windows are failing, I'll tell you so, and we do those.

sections.heading: Basement and Egress Windows
body: The small windows below grade get ignored, and they take a beating: ground moisture, lawn mowers, dirt packed against the frame. Old ones leak, rot the framing around them and let in cold air all winter.
We replace basement windows and egress windows and seal them in. An egress window is the one a person has to be able to climb out of, so it matters that it opens properly.

sections.quote: John was very knowledgeable in his work. He replaced a basement window for me. Not only did they finish the job in a quick time frame but was cheaper than all the other contractors by far. I highly recommend them and will be using them again.

sections.heading: Sliding Glass and Entry Doors
body: An old sliding glass door is usually the leakiest opening in the house. The rollers wear down, the track bends, and the seal where the panels meet stops sealing.
You end up shoving it open with your shoulder and feeling the draft all winter. A new slider glides and shuts tight.
We install sliding glass doors and entry doors by themselves or with your windows, so the glass, frames and trim all match.

sections.quote: Working with John was simple, fast and friendly. He made choosing a sliding glass door easy and affordable. Really happy with his crew too.

sections.heading: What Install Day Looks Like
body: Before anything is ordered, every opening gets measured, because a replacement window has to fit the opening that's actually there, not the one on the plans. Older Wichita houses often have openings that are slightly out of square.
On install day the crew takes out the old window, checks the opening, sets the new one level, seals it and trims it so it matches your exterior. The old windows and the trash leave with them.
A set of windows is typically a one-day job. John tells you how long yours will take when he gives you the price.

sections.quote: We are extremely happy with our new windows. The original estimate had no hidden fees. The workers showed up on time the day of installation and were very efficient & friendly. The windows were installed in one day and they cleaned up yard & inside when they were done.
sections.name: Becky E.

items.q: Do I have to replace every window?
items.a: No. Some houses need all of them, some need two or three. I'll look at each and tell you which are worth replacing.

items.q: What does a window replacement cost?
items.a: It depends on how many windows, their sizes and the style you choose. I give you the price in writing after I see the house, and the estimate is free.

items.q: Will new windows lower my energy bills?
items.a: A tight window stops the draft and the air leaking around it, so the house holds its temperature. How much you save depends on how bad the old ones were. Darby M. noticed a difference in her bills that first spring.

items.q: What if there's rot around a window?
items.a: Soft wood at the sill or frame is common behind old, leaking windows. If we find it, that's extra work, it gets its own price, and the new window goes into sound wood.
Financing is available, subject to credit approval.

sections.heading: Signs Your Siding Is Done
body: Siding takes the Kansas wind, hail and summer sun before anything else on the house does. After enough years it shows.

Look for cracked or warped panels, boards that have rotted at the bottom edge, chalky or badly faded color, and pieces the wind keeps loosening. Look inside, too. A stain on a ceiling or a damp corner in a room along an outside wall means water is getting behind the siding.
That is the part that costs money. Siding is the outer layer that sheds water, and the wall behind it, the sheathing and the framing, is what rots when the siding stops doing that.

sections.heading: The Whole House, or Just the Walls That Need It
body: A lot of people assume siding is an all-or-nothing job. It isn't.
If the siding on three sides is sound and one side was hit by hail or damaged by a leak, we can replace that side. Fixing a chimney or a garage wall is the same idea.
The trade-off is color and age: new panels next to siding that has weathered for twenty years can look different, and I'll tell you if that's going to bother you.

When the whole house needs it, we replace the whole house, and the old siding is hauled away. We work in vinyl and fiber cement, and I'll show you what each costs and how each wears before you choose.

sections.quote: I called three different companies out for estimates to repair the siding on our chimney, and Greenway was 25-35% cheaper than both the alternatives. John was able to get his crew out to work on the job within the week and got it finished up that day, and chimney looks great!

sections.heading: Siding Repair
body: Not every problem is a replacement. Rotted boards, a section the wind took, storm damage, siding around a chimney or a window that has pulled loose: these are repairs, and they're priced as repairs.
A repair makes sense when the rest of the siding still has years left. If it's failing everywhere, patching only buys time, and I'll say so.

sections.heading: Fascia, Soffit and Trim
body: The fascia is the board along the edge of your roof, the soffit is the underside of the overhang, and trim goes around the windows, doors and corners. When they go soft or pull away, water gets behind the gutters and animals find a way into the attic.
We replace them along with your siding, so the roof edge matches the new walls. We also repair single pieces. Gutters and exterior painting are done the same way, alongside the siding or windows.

sections.quote: Had a long piece of aluminum fascia trim blow off in a severe windstorm. Left a message with Greenway Exteriors and John called same day. They were able to come out in 2 days and were able to fabricate a replacement piece on site with the actual textured aluminum material. The price was very reasonable.
sections.name: Mark H.

sections.heading: What Replacement Looks Like
body: The crew takes off the old siding and looks at the wall underneath before anything new goes on. Damaged sheathing gets fixed. Then the new siding goes up, the trim is finished and the old material goes into the truck.
Crews start early and work until the light is gone. A whole house takes days, not weeks, and you get the schedule when I give you the price.

sections.quote: I just had my house resided, the crew was excellent. They did it in 4 days, these guys didn't waste any daylight. They worked from morning to dark. They were very professional, very respectful of my property, answered any questions, and asked questions. When they were finished, their clean up was so good, the only way you knew they had been here, was the beautiful job they did with the siding.

items.q: How do I know if I need new siding or just a repair?
items.a: If the damage is on one wall or one spot and the rest is sound, it's a repair. If it's cracking, warping or fading across the house, or water has been getting in, replacement is the better money. I look at the whole house before I tell you which.

items.q: Can you replace just one side of the house?
items.a: Yes. Color match is the one thing to talk through, and I'll tell you what I think when I see it.
It depends on the size of the house, the material and what's behind the old siding. I give you the price after I see it, and the estimate is free.

items.q: What if you find rot once the old siding is off?
items.a: That's extra work, and it gets its own price. It's the one thing nobody can see until the siding comes off.
